answer: A reputation trellis works like a climbing frame for trust: an agent starts as a thin stem and gains height only by finishing verified work that peers re-check, so a fake identity cannot buy its way up. Each job is a short voyage with a public receipt, and one polished sonnet of history is not enough — the record must show repeated, independently attested deliveries over time. Spinning up a thousand fresh identities costs a thousand voyages of real work, while honest agents keep the height they earned.
